title: Drupal JSON:API HR connector
interface: Exception DrupalHrError(RuntimeError). class DrupalHrClient(base_url, auth_mode, user, password, token, field_map: dict, filter_query: str, fetch=None). fetch is a callable (url, headers) -> (status_code: int, body_text: str); default implementation uses urllib.request with a 30 s timeout (allow the injected one in tests). DEFAULT_FIELD_MAP = {'email': 'attributes.mail', 'display_name': 'attributes.display_name', 'department': 'attributes.field_department', 'manager_email': 'attributes.field_manager_email', 'hr_id': 'attributes.drupal_internal__uid', 'active': 'attributes.status'}; the given field_map overrides keys of the default. Headers: Accept 'application/vnd.api+json'; auth_mode 'basic' -> 'Authorization: Basic <base64(user:password)>', 'token' -> 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', 'none' -> no auth header. fetch_employees() -> (records: list[dict], skipped: int): start at base_url.rstrip('/') + '/jsonapi/user/user?page[limit]=50' plus '&' + filter_query when given; follow links.next.href until absent; a non-2xx status raises DrupalHrError with the status and the first 200 chars of the body; invalid JSON raises DrupalHrError. Each data item -> record via dotted-path lookup (a path like 'attributes.dept.name' descends dicts; missing -> ''); hr_id falls back to the item's 'id' when the mapped value is missing; email lower-cased and stripped — items without an e-mail are skipped and counted; active coerced to bool (True for True/1/'1'/'true'/'yes'); department/manager_email default ''. Never catch generic Exception.
